title: 两节 RC 低通电路的网络函数
statement: 两节相同的 RC 低通电路直接级联：R₁ = R₂ = R = 1 kΩ，C₁ = C₂ = C = 1 µF，输出端 o 开路。H(jω) = V̇_o/V̇_s。
取 ω = 1/(RC) = 1000 rad/s。求 |V_a/V_s|、|H(jω)| 和 H(jω) 的相位。再和“两节互不影响”的情况比较。

questions.explain: H = −j/3，相位 −90°。一般式 H = 1/(1 − (ωRC)² + j3ωRC)，ωRC = 1 时实部为零。

questions.ask: 如果在 a 点后插入理想电压跟随器，使第二节不再从第一节取电流，ω = 1/(RC) 时 |H| 变为多少？
choices: 不变（和直接级联时一样）
choiceExplain: “不变”只对直接级联成立：那时第二节从第一节取电流。插入跟随器后负载效应消失，|V_a/V_s| 回到 1/√2。
1/√2 只是一节的 |H|，忘了乘上第二节的 1/√2。
1/4 是把每节当成了电阻分压：把 R 和 X_C 的大小直接相加，单节得 1000/(1000 + 1000) = 1/2。R 与 C 上的电压相差 90°，要用复阻抗：单节是 |1/(1 + j)| = 1/√2。
questions.explain: 隔离后两节各自 H₁ = H₂ = 1/(1 + j)，|H| = (1/√2)² = 1/2，相位 −90°。直接级联时第二节是第一节的负载，|V_a/V_s| 从 0.7071 降到 0.4714，总的 |H| 从 1/2 降到 1/3。网络函数不能简单地把各节“单独算的” H 相乘，除非后级不取电流。

hints: 先算 a 点右边的等效阻抗：C₁ 与 (R₂ + C₂) 并联，再对 R₁ 分压得 V_a。
第二节开路，V̇_o/V̇_a = 1/(1 + jωRC)；最后 H = (V_a/V_s)·(V_o/V_a)。
solution: **5. 比较。** 两节互不影响时 |H| = 1/2；直接级联由于负载效应只有 1/3。

en.title: Network function of a two-section RC low-pass
statement: Two identical RC low-pass sections are cascaded directly: R₁ = R₂ = R = 1 kΩ, C₁ = C₂ = C = 1 µF, and the output o is open. H(jω) = V̇_o/V̇_s.
Take ω = 1/(RC) = 1000 rad/s. Find |V_a/V_s|, |H(jω)| and the phase of H(jω). Then compare with the case where the sections don't affect each other.

questions.explain: Looking right from a: Z₂ = R + 1/(jωC) = 1000 − j1000 Ω, in parallel with C₁ (−j1000 Ω) gives Z_p = 200 − j600 Ω. V̇_a/V̇_s = Z_p/(R + Z_p) = (200 − j600)/(1200 − j600) = (1 − j)/3, magnitude √2/3 ≈ 0.4714.
Second-section divider: V̇_o/V̇_a = 1/(1 + jωRC) = 1/(1 + j). H = (1 − j)/3 × 1/(1 + j) = −j/3, |H| = 1/3.
H = −j/3, phase −90°. In general H = 1/(1 − (ωRC)² + j3ωRC), whose real part vanishes at ωRC = 1.

questions.ask: If an ideal voltage follower is inserted after a, so that the second section draws no current from the first, what does |H| become at ω = 1/(RC)?
choices: unchanged (the same as the direct cascade)
choiceExplain: 'Unchanged' holds only for the direct cascade, where the second section draws current from the first. With the follower the loading disappears and |V_a/V_s| returns to 1/√2.
1/√2 is one section's |H|; the second section's 1/√2 has not been multiplied in.

1/4 treats each section as a resistive divider: adding the sizes of R and X_C directly gives 1000/(1000 + 1000) = 1/2 per section. The voltages on R and C are 90° apart, so complex impedances are needed: one section gives |1/(1 + j)| = 1/√2.
questions.explain: With a buffer each section has H₁ = H₂ = 1/(1 + j), so |H| = (1/√2)² = 1/2 with phase −90°. Cascaded directly, the second section loads the first: |V_a/V_s| drops from 0.7071 to 0.4714 and the overall |H| from 1/2 to 1/3. You can't just multiply the sections' stand-alone H's unless the later stage draws no current.

hints: First find the impedance to the right of a: C₁ in parallel with (R₂ + C₂); then use the divider with R₁ to get V_a.
The second section is unloaded, so V̇_o/V̇_a = 1/(1 + jωRC); finally H = (V_a/V_s)·(V_o/V_a).
solution: **4. Network function.** H = (1 − j)/3 · 1/(1 + j) = −j/3: |H| = **1/3**, phase **−90°**. In general H(jω) = 1/(1 − ω²R²C² + j3ωRC), which is 1/(j3) at ω = 1/(RC).
**5. Comparison.** If the sections didn't interact, |H| would be 1/2; cascaded directly the loading effect brings it down to 1/3.
